planner_self_verification.why: v2 defect 3 was a wrong factual claim about PostgreSQL rendering asserted without probing. Before submitting v3 the planner probed every new SQL claim on the live PostgreSQL 16.14 container rather than reasoning from memory.
results: regexp_count exists (PG15+) and returns 2 for a duplicated JSON key, 1 for a single key.
A duplicate key does collapse at ::jsonb, last value winning: {"name":"x","name":"y"} yields "y". The count check therefore has to inspect the raw text, as the plan specifies.
jsonb_typeof returns number for 7 while ->> coerces the same value to the text 7 — the exact laundering path defect 4 identified; the type gate must run first, as the plan specifies.

Digest binding is well-defined: sha256 over the stored canonical text is 4d88235c... while sha256 over the same document rendered by PostgreSQL ::text is d88776d5... The two genuinely differ, so probe D-25b cannot pass vacuously and the defect-3 premise is confirmed.
Exact key-set comparison via array_agg over jsonb_object_keys detects an extra top-level key.

The duplicate-key regexp has no false positives: a value containing the literal text "domain_label": still counts 1, because JSON escapes the inner quotes; and a key that is a substring of another key (key vs asset_key) counts 1 each, because the opening quote anchors the boundary.
planner_self_verification.correction: The claim recorded earlier — that the duplicate-key regexp "has no false positives" — was true as far as it went and misleading as a soundness claim. The probe set covered a value mimicking a key and a key that is a substring of another key, but NOT a Unicode-escaped key name. The reviewer probed that case and it is a real bypass, re-verified by the planner on PostgreSQL 16.14: for {"asset_key":"bad","\u0061sset_key":"good"}, regexp_count returns 1 while json_each decodes two asset_key entries and JSONB keeps "good" — so the DB verifies "good" while the human-visible canonical text says "bad", defeating the premise that the canonical bytes are the identity. Also re-verified: reordered check-result text is JSONB-equal to the canonical form, byte-different, and digest-self-consistent, so nothing in the specified guard forces actual canonical ordering. Incomplete verification is not verification; the record is corrected rather than left standing.

what_changed: Identity is the row, not a hash. Because the tables are append-only a row never changes, so a foreign key to catalog_assets.id is already a binding to immutable content. identity_canonical_json, the content_hash CHECK, and the deferrable rebind trigger are deleted outright — with them go the escaped-key, duplicate-key, type-coercion and extra-key evasions.

Vetting results are typed child rows keyed UNIQUE(record, check_name), not a JSONB array with a canonical-text column and a digest. No serialization exists, so none can be non-canonical. Cardinality and outcome derivation are dual deferred triggers, the Slice-37/40 pattern.

Provenance renamed to what it is: checker_output_admin_recorded and reviewer_asserted_admin_recorded. The plan states plainly that the DB cannot see which code produced a payload and that the label is app-stamped.
The AST tool-scope equality check is dropped entirely rather than patched a third time. Declared scope is declared and unverified, and the permission-scoped claim is refused.
The only digest retained, reference intake content_sha256, is labelled registrar-supplied drift-detection metadata and explicitly not authenticity or non-repudiation, per the owner's constraint.
